comparisons.peer_topic: Global Technology Scope and Product Portfolio
comparisons.peer_summary: Avago is a global technology leader designing semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, including AI networking, home connectivity, and software for mainframe and cloud platforms, while also offering fibre channel storage area networking products.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Avago define their core business model around the design and supply of semiconductor solutions, though Avago explicitly includes infrastructure software in its primary identity while Intel separates its foundry manufacturing scope. Intel describes itself as a 'global designer and manufacturer of semiconductor products... manufactured via our Intel Foundry operations and other suppliers,' highlighting its dual IDM and foundry role. In contrast, Avago defines itself as a 'global technology leader that designs, develops and supplies a broad range of semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions,' focusing on the breadth of its product portfolio including AI networking and software, without emphasizing internal manufacturing as part of the primary business model definition.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center customer segments and automotive demand outlook
comparisons.peer_summary: In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024, large cloud providers represented more than half of Data Center revenue. Additionally, the company expects NVIDIA's automotive data center processing demand to grow significantly as AV algorithms shift to video transformers.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures identify 'Data Centers' as a critical and dominant driver of business revenue and strategic focus, reflecting the industry's shift toward AI and cloud infrastructure. Intel explicitly mentions expanding its Intel Foundry business to serve 'external customers' (implied to include cloud/AI providers) in its business model overview. Similarly, Nvidia details that 'large cloud providers represented more than half of our Data Center revenue' in Q4 2024, underscoring the centrality of this customer segment. While Intel frames this through the lens of manufacturing capacity and foundry expansion, Nvidia frames it through the lens of specific revenue concentration and demand drivers for its networking and compute products.

sentences.text: We seek to expand our Intel Foundry business as a third-party foundry for external customers.
In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024, large cloud providers represented more than half of our Data Center revenue, supporting both internal workloads and external customers.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm operates through three reportable segments: QCT (semiconductor), QTL (licensing), and QSI (strategic investments), along with nonreportable segments like QGOV.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm use segment reporting to delineate their business models, contrasting Intel's operational split between 'Intel Products' (marketing/sales) and 'Intel Foundry' (manufacturing) with Qualcomm's product and service-based segments (QCT, QTL, QSI). Intel's disclosure states products are 'primarily marketed and sold through our Intel Products business and manufactured via our Intel Foundry operations,' defining the business by its supply chain structure. Qualcomm, conversely, organizes by 'products and services' into QCT (semiconductor sales), QTL (licensing), and QSI (investments), defining the business by revenue generation methods rather than manufacturing vs. design separation.
